# Rule catalogue

<!-- Generated by `envleak rules --markdown`. Do not edit by hand; edit
     internal/rules/rules.yaml and run `make docs`. -->

65 rules, grouped by tag. Every rule below is covered by at least one
positive and one negative test case, taken from the examples in this file.

## Confidence

A finding's confidence is derived from which engines agreed:

| Situation | Confidence |
|---|---|
| Pattern hit on a prefix-anchored format, checksum validated | `high` |
| Pattern hit on a prefix-anchored format, no validator | `high` |
| Pattern hit whose entropy check passed | one level up from the rule's base |
| Pattern hit whose entropy check failed | one level down |
| Pattern hit whose checksum failed | one level down (never dropped) |
| Found in a test, doc, example, lockfile or generated file | one level down |
| Entropy engine alone, no pattern | `low` |

## Validators

| Validator | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `github-crc32` | Recomputes the base62 CRC32 checksum in the last 6 characters of a prefixed GitHub token (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`) over the preceding 30. |
| `github-pat-structure` | Verifies the shape of a fine-grained PAT: `github_pat_` + 22 base62 + `_` + 59 base62. GitHub publishes no checksum for this format. |
| `jwt` | Base64url-decodes the first segment and requires valid JSON carrying a non-empty `alg` claim, which rejects unrelated blobs that merely start with `eyJ`. |

## Continuation checks

Some matches only mean something in the light of the *next* line. A rule
declaring a `continuation` has its match held back one line and dropped if
the check fails, which is how a PEM banner quoted in a README stays quiet
while the same banner followed by base64 does not.

| Check | What it requires of the following line |
|---|---|
| `pem-body` | Base64 key material (at least 32 characters) or an RFC 1421 header such as `Proc-Type:`. A banner at end of file, or followed by prose, is dropped. |

## Adding a rule

1. Add an entry to `internal/rules/rules.yaml`.
2. Give it at least one `positive` and one `negative` example — `TestRuleExamples`
   enforces both, so a rule that does not work cannot be merged.
3. Pick `keywords` that appear in every real match: the Aho-Corasick prefilter
   only runs your regex on lines containing one of them.
4. Run `make test docs`.
